claim: Malaria-071 demonstrated that administration of three doses of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine given at one-month intervals resulted in 62.5% protection.
source: Malaria-071, a controlled human malaria infection trial, demonstrated that administration of three doses of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine given at one-month intervals was inferior to a delayed fractional dose (DFD) schedule (62.5% vs 86.7% protection, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the protection rate for the standard dosing regimen in the abstract.

claim: Malaria-071 demonstrated that a delayed fractional dose (DFD) schedule of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine resulted in 86.7% protection.
source: Malaria-071, a controlled human malaria infection trial, demonstrated that administration of three doses of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine given at one-month intervals was inferior to a delayed fractional dose (DFD) schedule (62.5% vs 86.7% protection, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the protection rate for the DFD regimen in the abstract.

claim: Protection in both vaccine arms was associated with early induction of functional IL-21-secreting circumsporozoite (CSP)-specific pTfh cells.
source: Here, we show that protection in both study arms was associated with early induction of functional IL-21-secreting circumsporozoite (CSP)-specific pTfh cells, together with induction of CSP-specific memory B cell responses after the second dose that persisted after the third dose.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study's analysis.

claim: Protection in both vaccine arms was associated with induction of CSP-specific memory B cell responses after the second dose that persisted after the third dose.
source: Here, we show that protection in both study arms was associated with early induction of functional IL-21-secreting circumsporozoite (CSP)-specific pTfh cells, together with induction of CSP-specific memory B cell responses after the second dose that persisted after the third dose.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study's analysis.

claim: A subset of non-protected individuals in the standard (STD) vaccine arm lost prior protective B cell responses after receiving the third vaccine dose.
source: Data integration of key immunologic measures identified a subset of non-protected individuals in the standard (STD) vaccine arm who lost prior protective B cell responses after receiving the third vaccine dose.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from data integration analysis.

claim: The DFD regimen favors persistence of functional B cells after the third dose.
source: We conclude that the DFD regimen favors persistence of functional B cells after the third dose.
evidence: This is stated as the main conclusion in the abstract.

claim: In 2017, malaria cases were reported to occur in 87 countries with an estimated 435,000 deaths of children under the age of five.
source: In 2017, malaria cases were reported to occur in 87 countries with an estimated 435,000 deaths of children under the age of five (WHO, 2018).
evidence: This statistic is cited from WHO, 2018.

claim: There is currently no licensed malaria vaccine.
source: Development of a protective vaccine has been challenging and currently there is no licensed malaria vaccine.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the introduction.

claim: The RTS,S/AS01 vaccine is the most advanced malaria vaccine in development.
source: Among vaccines in development, the RTS,S/AS01 vaccine is the most advanced and is now part of a large-scale pilot implementation program in children in selected African countries.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the introduction.

claim: The RTS,S/AS01 vaccine is now part of a large-scale pilot implementation program in children in selected African countries.
source: Among vaccines in development, the RTS,S/AS01 vaccine is the most advanced and is now part of a large-scale pilot implementation program in children in selected African countries.
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the introduction.

claim: The RTS,S/AS01 vaccine includes portions of the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of Plasmodium falciparum.
source: This vaccine includes three main components: a) portions of the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of Plasmodium falciparum, which is the primary surface antigen (Ag) on the sporozoites; b) hepatitis B surface antigen (HB); and c) a proprietary AS01B adjuvant from GlaxoSmithKline (GSK).
evidence: The vaccine composition is described in the introduction.

claim: CSP is the primary surface antigen on Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites.
source: This vaccine includes three main components: a) portions of the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of Plasmodium falciparum, which is the primary surface antigen (Ag) on the sporozoites; b) hepatitis B surface antigen (HB); and c) a proprietary AS01B adjuvant from GlaxoSmithKline (GSK).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about CSP in the introduction.

claim: The RTS,S/AS01 vaccine includes hepatitis B surface antigen (HB).
source: This vaccine includes three main components: a) portions of the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of Plasmodium falciparum, which is the primary surface antigen (Ag) on the sporozoites; b) hepatitis B surface antigen (HB); and c) a proprietary AS01B adjuvant from GlaxoSmithKline (GSK).
evidence: The vaccine composition is described in the introduction.

claim: The RTS,S/AS01 vaccine includes a proprietary AS01B adjuvant from GlaxoSmithKline (GSK).
source: This vaccine includes three main components: a) portions of the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) of Plasmodium falciparum, which is the primary surface antigen (Ag) on the sporozoites; b) hepatitis B surface antigen (HB); and c) a proprietary AS01B adjuvant from GlaxoSmithKline (GSK).
evidence: The vaccine composition is described in the introduction.

claim: The AS01B adjuvant is composed of 3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) from Salmonella minnesota and a saponin molecule (QS-21) purified from an extract from the plant Quillaja saponaria.
source: The adjuvant is composed of 3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) from Salmonella minnesota and a saponin molecule (QS-21) purified from an extract from the plant Quillaja saponaria, combined in a liposomal formulation consisting of dioleoyl phosphatidylcholine and cholesterol in phosphate-buffered saline solution (Vekemans et al., 2009).
evidence: The adjuvant composition is cited from Vekemans et al., 2009.

claim: The AS01B adjuvant is combined in a liposomal formulation consisting of dioleoyl phosphatidylcholine and cholesterol in phosphate-buffered saline solution.
source: The adjuvant is composed of 3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) from Salmonella minnesota and a saponin molecule (QS-21) purified from an extract from the plant Quillaja saponaria, combined in a liposomal formulation consisting of dioleoyl phosphatidylcholine and cholesterol in phosphate-buffered saline solution (Vekemans et al., 2009).
evidence: The adjuvant formulation is cited from Vekemans et al., 2009.

claim: A vaccine delivery regimen in which three doses of RTS,S/AS01B are given on a 0, 1, 2 month schedule was found to provide nearly 50% protection in controlled human malaria infection (CHMI) trials.
source: A vaccine delivery regimen in which three doses of RTS,S/AS01B are given on a 0, 1, 2 month schedule was found to provide nearly 50% protection in controlled human malaria infection (CHMI) trials (Kester et al., 2009; Ockenhouse et al., 2015).
evidence: This finding is cited from Kester et al., 2009 and Ockenhouse et al., 2015.

claim: A Phase 3 trial of RTS,S/AS01 vaccine using the 0, 1, 2 month dosing schedule showed only modest efficacy of 30.1% in 6–12-week-old infants.
source: In the field, however, a Phase 3 trial of RTS,S/AS01 vaccine using the same dosing schedule showed only modest efficacy of 30.1% in 6–12-week-old infants (Agnandji et al., 2012).
evidence: This finding is cited from Agnandji et al., 2012.

claim: Malaria-071 (NCT01857869) was designed to compare the standard (STD) 0, 1, 2 month dosing regimen with a delayed fractional dose (DFD) regimen in which the third dose was one fifth of the standard dose and was administered at 7 months after the second dose.
source: In search of better efficacy, a recent CHMI trial of RTS,S/AS01 vaccine (Malaria-071, NCT01857869) was designed to compare the standard (STD) 0, 1, 2 month dosing regimen with a delayed fractional dose (DFD) regimen in which the third dose was one fifth of the standard dose and was administered at 7 months after the second dose (Regules et al., 2016).
evidence: The study design is cited from Regules et al., 2016.

claim: The rationale for testing the DFD regimen was based on a prior study from 1997 that had found that delaying and reducing the third immunization dose enhanced the immunogenicity of RTS,S vaccine and achieved efficacy to 86%.
source: The rationale for testing the DFD regimen was based on a prior study from 1997 that had found that delaying and reducing the third immunization dose enhanced the immunogenicity of RTS,S vaccine and achieved efficacy to 86% (Stoute et al., 1997).
evidence: This rationale is cited from Stoute et al., 1997.

claim: Malaria-071 confirmed that the DFD regimen showed 86% efficacy.
source: Interestingly, Malaria-071 confirmed the earlier findings and the DFD regimen again showed 86% efficacy, which was significantly greater than the 62.5% protection observed in the STD regimen.
evidence: This finding is stated in the introduction.

claim: The DFD regimen efficacy of 86% was significantly greater than the 62.5% protection observed in the STD regimen.
source: Interestingly, Malaria-071 confirmed the earlier findings and the DFD regimen again showed 86% efficacy, which was significantly greater than the 62.5% protection observed in the STD regimen.
evidence: This comparison is stated in the introduction.

claim: A prior CHMI trial of the RTS,S vaccine found an association of anti-CSP antibody titers and CSP-specific CD4 T cells with protection.
source: The present study focused on assessing the role of peripheral T follicular helper (pTfh) cells and B cells, because a prior CHMI trial of the RTS,S vaccine had found an association of anti-CSP antibody titers and CSP-specific CD4 T cells with protection (White et al., 2013).
evidence: This finding is cited from White et al., 2013.

claim: In Malaria-071, antibodies of higher avidity were elicited in the DFD regimen in association with higher somatic hypermutation of B cells.
source: In Malaria-071, antibodies of higher avidity were elicited in the DFD regimen in association with higher somatic hypermutation of B cells, suggesting fundamental changes in the maturation of B cell affinity (Regules et al., 2016).
evidence: This finding is cited from Regules et al., 2016.

claim: High-affinity antibodies are generated from long-lived plasma cells and memory B cells that are produced after antigen-primed B cells undergo cognate interaction with T follicular helper cells (Tfh).
source: High-affinity antibodies are generated from long-lived plasma cells and memory B cells that are produced after antigen-primed B cells undergo cognate interaction with T follicular helper cells (Tfh).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: T follicular helper cell and B cell interaction occurs in the germinal centers (GC) of secondary lymphoid organs.
source: This interaction occurs in the germinal centers (GC) of secondary lymphoid organs (reviewed in Crotty, 2011), causing the B cells to proliferate followed by isotype switching and somatic hypermutation.
evidence: This is cited from a review by Crotty, 2011.

claim: Tfh-B cell interaction causes B cells to proliferate followed by isotype switching and somatic hypermutation.
source: This interaction occurs in the germinal centers (GC) of secondary lymphoid organs (reviewed in Crotty, 2011), causing the B cells to proliferate followed by isotype switching and somatic hypermutation.
evidence: This is cited from a review by Crotty, 2011.

claim: Many properties of lymphoid Tfh cells, including B cell helper function for antibody generation, are also present in a subset of circulating CD4 T cells designated as pTfh cells.
source: Many properties of lymphoid Tfh cells, including B cell helper function for antibody (Ab) generation (Crotty, 2011), are also present in a subset of circulating CD4 T cells designated as pTfh cells that are considered as having emigrated from the lymphoid pool into the peripheral circulation (Vella et al., 2019; Pahwa, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Crotty, 2011; Vella et al., 2019; Pahwa, 2019.

claim: pTfh cells are considered as having emigrated from the lymphoid pool into the peripheral circulation.
source: Many properties of lymphoid Tfh cells, including B cell helper function for antibody (Ab) generation (Crotty, 2011), are also present in a subset of circulating CD4 T cells designated as pTfh cells that are considered as having emigrated from the lymphoid pool into the peripheral circulation (Vella et al., 2019; Pahwa, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Vella et al., 2019; Pahwa, 2019.

claim: pTfh in circulation serve as an attractive alternative to lymphoid Tfh for investigating their role in human vaccine trials.
source: To investigate their role in human vaccine trials, pTfh in circulation serve as an attractive alternative to lymphoid Tfh, which require lymph node biopsies (Bentebibel et al., 2016; Bentebibel et al., 2013; Herati et al., 2017; Herati et al., 2014; Pallikkuth et al., 2017; Pallikkuth et al., 2012; Pallikkuth et al., 2019; Boswell et al., 2014; Cubas et al., 2013; Locci et al., 2013; Simpson et al., 2010; Ueno, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Lymphoid Tfh require lymph node biopsies for investigation.
source: To investigate their role in human vaccine trials, pTfh in circulation serve as an attractive alternative to lymphoid Tfh, which require lymph node biopsies (Bentebibel et al., 2016; Bentebibel et al., 2013; Herati et al., 2017; Herati et al., 2014; Pallikkuth et al., 2017; Pallikkuth et al., 2012; Pallikkuth et al., 2019; Boswell et al., 2014; Cubas et al., 2013; Locci et al., 2013; Simpson et al., 2010; Ueno, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a fact with multiple citations.

claim: In a murine model, a nanoparticle-based vaccine presenting recombinant P. vivax CSP led to a protective immune response, characterized by enhanced GC formation with expansion and differentiation of antigen-specific Tfh cells.
source: In a murine model, a nanoparticle-based vaccine presenting recombinant P. vivax CSP led to a protective immune response, characterized by enhanced GC formation with expansion and differentiation of antigen-specific Tfh cells (Moon et al., 2012).
evidence: This finding is cited from Moon et al., 2012.

claim: A malaria vaccine study in humans involving RTS,S/AS01 showed that skewing of pTfh cells towards a CXCR3+ Th1 phenotype was associated with reduced Ab quantity and quality and lower vaccine efficacy.
source: A malaria vaccine study in humans involving RTS,S/AS01 alone or co-administered with different viral-vectored vaccines showed that skewing of pTfh cells towards a CXC chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3+) Th1 phenotype was associated with reduced Ab quantity and quality and lower vaccine efficacy (Bowyer et al., 2018).
evidence: This finding is cited from Bowyer et al., 2018.

claim: In a phase III trial of the GSK malaria vaccine 'Mosquirix' in Tanzania and Mozambique, children with increased frequencies of pTfh and plasmablasts at the time of vaccination exhibited higher Ab titers.
source: More recently, in a phase III trial of the GSK malaria vaccine 'Mosquirix' in Tanzania and Mozambique, children with increased frequencies of pTfh and plasmablasts at the time of vaccination exhibited higher Ab titers (Hill et al., 2020).
evidence: This finding is cited from Hill et al., 2020.

claim: An important role was ascribed to antigen-specific pTfh and their cytokine profile in influenza vaccine-induced antibody responses.
source: An important role was ascribed to antigen-specific pTfh and their cytokine profile in influenza vaccine-induced antibody responses (Pallikkuth et al., 2019).
evidence: This finding is cited from Pallikkuth et al., 2019.

claim: The distribution of protected/non-protected participants was 10/6 in the STD regimen, and 26/4 in the DFD regimen.
source: The distribution of protected (P)/non-protected (NP) participants was 10/6 in the STD regimen, and 26/4 in the DFD regimen (Regules et al., 2016).
evidence: This data is cited from Regules et al., 2016.

claim: Frequencies of total pTfh were greater at all the timepoints post-vaccination than at T0 in protected subjects.
source: Frequencies of total pTfh were greater at all the timepoints post-vaccination than at T0 in P subjects, and these frequencies showed sustained expansion after vaccination compared to NP subjects at T3, T4 T6 and T7 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Total pTfh frequencies showed sustained expansion after vaccination compared to NP subjects at T3, T4, T6 and T7.
source: Frequencies of total pTfh were greater at all the timepoints post-vaccination than at T0 in P subjects, and these frequencies showed sustained expansion after vaccination compared to NP subjects at T3, T4 T6 and T7 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Frequencies of CSP-specific CD4 T cells were significantly increased at T2–T7 compared to those at T0 in protected subjects.
source: Frequencies of CSP-specific CD4 T cells were significantly increased at T2–T7 compared to those at T0 in P subjects (Figure 2E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: CSP-specific pTfh cells showed a strong vaccine-induced expansion in protected subjects and were more numerous at all the timepoints post-vaccination than at T0.
source: CSP-specific pTfh cells showed a strong vaccine-induced expansion in P subjects and were more numerous at all the timepoints post-vaccination than at T0 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Neither total pTfh, CSP-specific CD4 nor CSP-specific pTfh cells showed an increase post-vaccination in non-protected subjects.
source: Importantly, neither total pTfh, CSP-specific CD4 nor CSP-specific pTfh cells showed an increase post-vaccination in NP subjects.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: At T5, T6 and T7, the frequencies of total pTfh, CSP-specific CD4 and CSP-specific pTfh did not show differences between the STD and DFD regimens.
source: At T5, T6 and T7, the late timepoints after the two regimens diverged, the frequencies of total pTfh, CSP-specific CD4 and CSP-specific pTfh did not show differences between the STD and DFD regimens (Figure 2G, H and I, respectively), but the frequencies of total pTfh and CSP-specific CD4 T cells in the DFD regimen showed a decline at T7, the last time point that was evaluated (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 2G, H, and I.

claim: The frequencies of total pTfh and CSP-specific CD4 T cells in the DFD regimen showed a decline at T7.
source: At T5, T6 and T7, the late timepoints after the two regimens diverged, the frequencies of total pTfh, CSP-specific CD4 and CSP-specific pTfh did not show differences between the STD and DFD regimens (Figure 2G, H and I, respectively), but the frequencies of total pTfh and CSP-specific CD4 T cells in the DFD regimen showed a decline at T7, the last time point that was evaluated (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 2G and H.

claim: A significant increase in the frequencies of IL-21-expressing CSP-specific pTfh cells was evident in protected subjects at all timepoints post vaccination.
source: A significant increase in the frequencies (compared to those at T0) of IL-21-expressing (Figure 3G) and ICOS+ (Figure 3H) CSP-specific pTfh cells was evident in P subjects at all timepoints post vaccination and of Ki67+ (Figure 3I) CSP-specific pTfh cells at T3–T7.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: A significant increase in the frequencies of ICOS+ CSP-specific pTfh cells was evident in protected subjects at all timepoints post vaccination.
source: A significant increase in the frequencies (compared to those at T0) of IL-21-expressing (Figure 3G) and ICOS+ (Figure 3H) CSP-specific pTfh cells was evident in P subjects at all timepoints post vaccination and of Ki67+ (Figure 3I) CSP-specific pTfh cells at T3–T7.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: A significant increase in the frequencies of Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh cells was evident in protected subjects at T3–T7.
source: A significant increase in the frequencies (compared to those at T0) of IL-21-expressing (Figure 3G) and ICOS+ (Figure 3H) CSP-specific pTfh cells was evident in P subjects at all timepoints post vaccination and of Ki67+ (Figure 3I) CSP-specific pTfh cells at T3–T7.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Frequencies of IL-21+ and ICOS+ CSP-specific pTfh cells showed an increase at T4, T6 and T7 in protected subjects compared to non-protected subjects.
source: When comparing CSP-specific pTfh of P to NP subjects, frequencies of IL-21+ and ICOS+ cells showed an increase at T4, T6 and T7 (Figure 3D and E) and a transient increase of Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh cells at T2 in P subjects (Figure 3F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 3D and E.

claim: Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh cells showed a transient increase at T2 in protected subjects compared to non-protected subjects.
source: When comparing CSP-specific pTfh of P to NP subjects, frequencies of IL-21+ and ICOS+ cells showed an increase at T4, T6 and T7 (Figure 3D and E) and a transient increase of Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh cells at T2 in P subjects (Figure 3F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: In non-protected subjects, no increase in IL-21+ or ICOS+ or in Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh was noted post-vaccination, and the levels remained at background levels.
source: In the NP subjects, no increase in IL-21+ or ICOS+ or in Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh was noted post-vaccination, and the levels remained at background levels (Figure 3D, E and F), with ICOS+ cells dipping even lower at T7 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 3D, E, and F.

claim: ICOS+ CSP-specific pTfh cells dipped even lower at T7 in non-protected subjects.
source: In the NP subjects, no increase in IL-21+ or ICOS+ or in Ki67+ CSP-specific pTfh was noted post-vaccination, and the levels remained at background levels (Figure 3D, E and F), with ICOS+ cells dipping even lower at T7 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: IL-21- and ICOS-expressing CSP-specific pTfh were significantly more frequent at T7 in the DFD regimen compared to the STD regimen.
source: Comparing the two regimens, we noticed that IL-21- and ICOS-expressing CSP-specific pTfh were significantly more frequent at T7 in the DFD regimen, but did not show a difference in Ki67 expression (Figure 3G, H and I, respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 3G and H.

claim: Ki67 expression in CSP-specific pTfh did not show a difference between the DFD and STD regimens at T7.
source: Comparing the two regimens, we noticed that IL-21- and ICOS-expressing CSP-specific pTfh were significantly more frequent at T7 in the DFD regimen, but did not show a difference in Ki67 expression (Figure 3G, H and I, respectively).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: In the STD regimen, the frequencies of IL-21+ CSP-specific pTfh decreased at T7 from those at T5 and T6.
source: In the STD regimen, the frequencies of IL-21+ CSP-specific pTfh decreased at T7 from those at T5 and T6 (Figure 3G).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Protected subjects show vaccination-induced expansion of both total and functional CSP-specific pTfh cells that respond to Ag stimulation with IL-21 production and ICOS and Ki67 expression.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that, as a group, P subjects show vaccination-induced expansion of both total and functional CSP-specific pTfh cells that respond to Ag stimulation with IL-21 production and ICOS and Ki67 expression, whereas NP subjects do not do so.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: Non-protected subjects do not show vaccination-induced expansion of both total and functional CSP-specific pTfh cells that respond to Ag stimulation with IL-21 production and ICOS and Ki67 expression.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that, as a group, P subjects show vaccination-induced expansion of both total and functional CSP-specific pTfh cells that respond to Ag stimulation with IL-21 production and ICOS and Ki67 expression, whereas NP subjects do not do so.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: Neither total B cells nor any of the ex-vivo-derived B cell maturation subsets differed significantly between protected vs. non-protected subjects at any timepoint.
source: Neither total B cells nor any of the ex-vivo-derived B cell maturation subsets differed significantly between P vs. NP subjects at any timepoint or between the two vaccine regimens at T5, T6 and T7 (not shown).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: Neither total B cells nor any of the ex-vivo-derived B cell maturation subsets differed significantly between the two vaccine regimens at T5, T6 and T7.
source: Neither total B cells nor any of the ex-vivo-derived B cell maturation subsets differed significantly between P vs. NP subjects at any timepoint or between the two vaccine regimens at T5, T6 and T7 (not shown).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: Regimen-specific differences in B cell phenotypes emerged post dose 3 (T5 or later) exclusively in the Ag-specific memory B cell compartment.
source: Changes in antigen-stimulated B cell phenotypes were noted mostly in relation to the regimen and not in the context of protection. Regimen-specific differences emerged post dose 3 (T5 or later) exclusively in the Ag-specific memory B cell compartment, including SM and sAM for PF-CSP (Figure 4A and B) and PF-16 (Figure 5D and E), with larger responses in the DFD arm compared to the STD arm.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4A, B and 5D, E.

claim: SM and sAM B cells for PF-CSP showed larger responses in the DFD arm compared to the STD arm at T5 or later.
source: Regimen-specific differences emerged post dose 3 (T5 or later) exclusively in the Ag-specific memory B cell compartment, including SM and sAM for PF-CSP (Figure 4A and B) and PF-16 (Figure 5D and E), with larger responses in the DFD arm compared to the STD arm.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4A and B.

claim: SM and sAM B cells for PF-16 showed larger responses in the DFD arm compared to the STD arm at T5 or later.
source: Regimen-specific differences emerged post dose 3 (T5 or later) exclusively in the Ag-specific memory B cell compartment, including SM and sAM for PF-CSP (Figure 4A and B) and PF-16 (Figure 5D and E), with larger responses in the DFD arm compared to the STD arm.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 5D and E.

claim: Ki67+ B cells were more frequent following PF-CSP and PF-16 antigen stimulation at T5 and T6 in the DFD arm.
source: Ki67+ B cells were also more frequent following PF-CSP and PF-16 antigen stimulation at T5 and T6 in the DFD arm (Figure 5C and F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 5C and F.

claim: A significant increase in the number of PF-CSP-specific spontaneous ASC were noted at day 6 post dose 2 (T3) in protected subjects but not in non-protected subjects.
source: A significant increase in the number of PF-CSP-specific (Figure 5A) and R32LR-specific (Figure 5B) spontaneous ASC were noted at day 6 post dose 2 (T3) in P subjects but not in NP subjects.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A significant increase in the number of R32LR-specific spontaneous ASC were noted at day 6 post dose 2 (T3) in protected subjects but not in non-protected subjects.
source: A significant increase in the number of PF-CSP-specific (Figure 5A) and R32LR-specific (Figure 5B) spontaneous ASC were noted at day 6 post dose 2 (T3) in P subjects but not in NP subjects.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Only protected subjects showed an increase in memory B cell response to PF-CSP protein from T0 to T4, T6 and T7.
source: Comparing P to NP subjects, we found that only the P subjects showed an increase in memory B cell response to PF-CSP protein from T0 to T4, T6 and T7, and that at these time points, both the PF-CSP response and the response to the PF16 region were greater in P than in NP subjects (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: At T4, T6 and T7, both the PF-CSP response and the response to the PF16 region were greater in protected than in non-protected subjects.
source: Comparing P to NP subjects, we found that only the P subjects showed an increase in memory B cell response to PF-CSP protein from T0 to T4, T6 and T7, and that at these time points, both the PF-CSP response and the response to the PF16 region were greater in P than in NP subjects (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figures 5C and D.

claim: The repeat region R32LR-specific memory B cell response increased in protected subjects only from T0 to T4 and T7.
source: The repeat region R32LR-specific memory B cell response also increased in P subjects only from T0 to T4 and T7, and was greater in the P group than in the NP group at T4 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The R32LR-specific memory B cell response was greater in the protected group than in the non-protected group at T4.
source: The repeat region R32LR-specific memory B cell response also increased in P subjects only from T0 to T4 and T7, and was greater in the P group than in the NP group at T4 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In the DFD regimen the memory B cell response to PF-CSP increased from T5 to T6 and T7.
source: Comparing the regimens, in the DFD regimen the memory B cell response to PF-CSP increased from T5 to T6 and T7 (Figure 5F), and the response to PF-16 at T7 (Figure 5G) was larger under the DFD regimen than under the STD regimen.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The memory B cell response to PF-16 at T7 was larger under the DFD regimen than under the STD regimen.
source: Comparing the regimens, in the DFD regimen the memory B cell response to PF-CSP increased from T5 to T6 and T7 (Figure 5F), and the response to PF-16 at T7 (Figure 5G) was larger under the DFD regimen than under the STD regimen.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: RTS,S/AS01 vaccination elicited strong, functionally competent CSP-specific memory B cell responses in the protected subjects, especially at the later timepoints.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that RTS,S/AS01 vaccination elicited strong, functionally competent CSP-specific memory B cell responses in the P subjects, especially at the later timepoints, and that these responses were larger in the DFD regimen and stronger for PF-16 than for R32LR.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: CSP-specific memory B cell responses were larger in the DFD regimen.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that RTS,S/AS01 vaccination elicited strong, functionally competent CSP-specific memory B cell responses in the P subjects, especially at the later timepoints, and that these responses were larger in the DFD regimen and stronger for PF-16 than for R32LR.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: CSP-specific memory B cell responses were stronger for PF-16 than for R32LR.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that RTS,S/AS01 vaccination elicited strong, functionally competent CSP-specific memory B cell responses in the P subjects, especially at the later timepoints, and that these responses were larger in the DFD regimen and stronger for PF-16 than for R32LR.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings.

claim: 676 of 1976 immune measures were significantly increased from baseline (T0) to different timepoints post-vaccine.
source: We identified 676 of 1976 immune measures that were significantly increased from baseline (T0) to different timepoints post-vaccine (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The 1976 immune features were grouped into 142 immune clusters, of which 40 clusters had at least one vaccine-antigen-specific immune feature.
source: By carrying out a correlation analysis to identify groups of correlated immune measures ('immune clusters'), we were able to group these 1976 immune features into 142 immune clusters, of which 40 clusters had at least one vaccine-antigen-specific immune feature.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The pTfh response was an early-stage response, emerging as early as T2, and persisting throughout the study.
source: Analysis of the vaccine-induced responses over the time course of the study revealed that the pTfh response was an early-stage response, emerging as early as T2, and persisting throughout the study.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The memory B cell response was a later-stage response, peaking between T4 and T5.
source: By contrast, the memory B cell response was a later-stage response, peaking between T4 and T5 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 65% to 80% of the immune responses classified as 'vaccine-induced' were specific to the vaccine antigens CSP or HBs.
source: 65% to 80% of the immune responses classified as 'vaccine-induced' were specific to the vaccine antigens CSP or HBs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), and the response was fairly balanced between both antigens.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The vaccine-induced response was fairly balanced between CSP and HBs antigens.
source: 65% to 80% of the immune responses classified as 'vaccine-induced' were specific to the vaccine antigens CSP or HBs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), and the response was fairly balanced between both antigens.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The random forest model using 41 parameters from timepoints prior to challenge (T6) achieved 85% accuracy with a kappa value of 0.63 in predicting vaccine regimen.
source: The LOO analysis shows that the random forest model, using these 41 parameters, achieved 85% accuracy with a kappa value of 0.63, indicating a strong predictive value.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: An average of 39 out of 46 subjects in the vaccine regimens were predicted correctly by the random forest model.
source: Overall, an average of 39 out of 46 subjects in the vaccine regimens were predicted correctly.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: Antigen-induced B cell characteristics, including proliferation (Ki67+) and frequencies of SM, sAM, and Ki67 expressing aMBC, were most predictive of regimen.
source: Further, we determined the relative importance of each parameter in the random forest (Table 1) and found that antigen-induced B cell characteristics, including proliferation (Ki67+) and frequencies of SM, sAM, and Ki67 expressing aMBC, were most predictive of regimen.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Table 1.

claim: Nearly all predictive parameters for regimen showed antigen specificity for either CSP (66%) or HBs (27%).
source: Nearly all predictive parameters showed antigen specificity for either CSP (66%) or HBs (27%).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The random forest model for predicting protection status achieved a predictive accuracy of 85% with a kappa of 0.45.
source: In order to predict protection status, we used 36 immune parameters that showed significant protection-level differences prior to challenge (T6 and earlier). We achieved a predictive accuracy of 85% with a kappa of 0.45, indicating low-to-moderate predictive ability, with 18 parameters in the model.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: 39 of 46 subjects were predicted correctly by the protection status model.
source: Overall, 39 of 46 subjects were predicted correctly.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The parameters that are most predictive of protection include CSP-specific CD40L+ CD4, HBs-specific IL-21+, CSP-specific pTfh, frequencies of total pTfh cells, and CSP-specific antibody-secreting memory B cells.
source: After analyzing for variable importance, we found that the parameters that are most predictive of protection (Table 2) include CSP-specific CD40L+ CD4, HBs-specific IL-21+, CSP-specific pTfh, frequencies of total pTfh cells, and CSP-specific antibody-secreting memory B cells.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Table 2.

claim: Many of the parameters most predictive of protection were from relatively early timepoints such as T2 and T4.
source: Of note, many of these parameters were from relatively early timepoints such as T2 and T4.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: Non-protected subjects clustered closely with each other and separately from protected subjects in PCA analysis.
source: We used PCA to visualize how well the predictive parameters identified in Table 2 could distinguish subjects by protection status (Figure 6B), and found that although there was a wide variability in the immune responses for P subjects, NP subjects clustered closely with each other and separately from P subjects.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: There is a distinct pattern of immune responses associated with vaccine failure in this study.
source: Together, these data suggest that there is a distinct pattern of immune responses associated with vaccine failure in this study.
evidence: This is an inference from the clustering analysis.

claim: The model trained on early-response data alone (post-dose 1 and 2) achieved 87% accuracy with a kappa of 0.46 in predicting protection.
source: We trained the model on early-response data alone (post-dose 1 and 2) to predict protection and achieved 87% accuracy with a kappa of 0.46, indicating moderate accuracy in predicting protection using only immune response data prior to dose 3.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The protection status of virtually all DFD subjects is predicted correctly using early-stage immune responses (97% accuracy, kappa = 0.84).
source: When we broke down the prediction results by vaccine regimen, we found that the protection status of virtually all DFD subjects is predicted correctly (97% accuracy, kappa = 0.84), whereas the protection status of STD subjects is predicted poorly (69% accuracy, Kappa = 0.26).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The protection status of STD subjects is predicted poorly using early-stage immune responses (69% accuracy, Kappa = 0.26).
source: When we broke down the prediction results by vaccine regimen, we found that the protection status of virtually all DFD subjects is predicted correctly (97% accuracy, kappa = 0.84), whereas the protection status of STD subjects is predicted poorly (69% accuracy, Kappa = 0.26).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: In both the STD regimen and the DFD regimen, approximately 15% of subjects elicited weak early-stage immune responses predictive of non-protection, and these subjects were subsequently found not to be protected following challenge.
source: Interestingly, in both the STD regimen and the DFD regimen, approximately 15% of subjects (dark orange) elicited weak early-stage immune responses predictive of non-protection, and these subjects were subsequently found not to be protected following challenge.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: Among DFD subjects, virtually all who elicited promising early-stage immune responses were in fact protected following dose 3 and challenge.
source: In terms of subjects who elicited promising early-stage immune responses, we found that among DFD subjects, virtually all were in fact protected following dose 3 and challenge.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: In the STD regimen, approximately one third of subjects with promising early-stage immune responses were not protected.
source: By contrast, in the STD regimen, approximately one third of subjects with promising early-stage immune responses were not protected.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text.

claim: The third immunization in the STD regimen may adversely affect the immune response elicited by dose 1 and dose 2, and this may lead to the lack of protection.
source: These findings suggest that the third immunization in the STD regimen may adversely affect the immune response elicited by dose 1 and dose 2, and this may lead to the lack of protection.
evidence: This is an inference from the prediction analysis.

claim: Study participants can be classified into three groups of outcomes: 'weak responders' (approximately 10–15% of subjects in both vaccine regimens, n = 6), who elicited poor early-stage immunogenicity and showed low efficacy (16% efficacy).
source: On the basis of these individualized predictions of efficacy constructed on the early-stage immune response data, we were able to classify study participants into three groups of outcomes (Figure 7A): 1) 'weak responders', approximately 10–15% of subjects in both vaccine regimens (n = 6), who elicited poor early-stage immunogenicity and showed low efficacy (16% efficacy); 2) 'DFD strong responders', DFD subjects who showed promising early-stage responses (n = 27) and were almost entirely protected (96% efficacy); and 3) 'STD strong responders', STD subjects who showed strong early responses (n = 13) and achieved moderate protection (70% efficacy).
evidence: This classification is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Study participants can be classified into three groups of outcomes: 'DFD strong responders', DFD subjects who showed promising early-stage responses (n = 27) and were almost entirely protected (96% efficacy).
source: On the basis of these individualized predictions of efficacy constructed on the early-stage immune response data, we were able to classify study participants into three groups of outcomes (Figure 7A): 1) 'weak responders', approximately 10–15% of subjects in both vaccine regimens (n = 6), who elicited poor early-stage immunogenicity and showed low efficacy (16% efficacy); 2) 'DFD strong responders', DFD subjects who showed promising early-stage responses (n = 27) and were almost entirely protected (96% efficacy); and 3) 'STD strong responders', STD subjects who showed strong early responses (n = 13) and achieved moderate protection (70% efficacy).
evidence: This classification is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Study participants can be classified into three groups of outcomes: 'STD strong responders', STD subjects who showed strong early responses (n = 13) and achieved moderate protection (70% efficacy).
source: On the basis of these individualized predictions of efficacy constructed on the early-stage immune response data, we were able to classify study participants into three groups of outcomes (Figure 7A): 1) 'weak responders', approximately 10–15% of subjects in both vaccine regimens (n = 6), who elicited poor early-stage immunogenicity and showed low efficacy (16% efficacy); 2) 'DFD strong responders', DFD subjects who showed promising early-stage responses (n = 27) and were almost entirely protected (96% efficacy); and 3) 'STD strong responders', STD subjects who showed strong early responses (n = 13) and achieved moderate protection (70% efficacy).
evidence: This classification is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The difference in efficacy between the DFD and STD regimens seemed to be accounted for entirely by a subset of early strong responders that failed to achieve protection in the STD regimen.
source: Finally, the difference in efficacy between the DFD and STD regimens seemed to be accounted for entirely by a subset of early strong responders that failed to achieve protection in the STD regimen.
evidence: This is an inference from the classification analysis.

claim: Protected subjects in both vaccine regimens were characterized by early induction of CSP antigen-specific pTfh responses, followed by functional memory B cell responses preceding the third dose that persisted at later time points.
source: We found that protected subjects in both vaccine regimens were characterized by early induction of CSP antigen-specific pTfh responses, followed by functional memory B cell responses preceding the third dose that persisted at later time points.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion.

claim: The non-protected subjects in both the DFD and STD regimens failed to mount the early pTfh response or B cell responses.
source: The non-protected subjects in both the DFD and STD regimens failed to mount the early pTfh response or B cell responses, pointing to the importance of pTfh in vaccine-induced protection.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion.

claim: In some non-protected subjects in the STD regimen, an initial 'protective' type of immune response was elicited by doses 1 and 2, but was aborted following the third vaccination dose.
source: A key finding that provided insight into the inferiority of STD regimen was that in some NP subjects an initial 'protective' type of immune response was elicited by doses 1 and 2, but was aborted following the third vaccination dose.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the Discussion.

claim: A clear increase in total pTfh cells and CSP-specific pTfh cells occurred as early as 6 days post-first dose of RTS,S/AS01 vaccination only in participants who were protected following experimental challenge with P. falciparum.
source: We noticed a clear increase in total pTfh cells and CSP-specific pTfh cells as early as 6 days post-first dose of RTS,S/AS01 vaccination that occurred only in participants who were protected following experimental challenge with P. falciparum.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion.

claim: Studies in healthy adults have documented the importance of pTfh expansion at day 7 or day 28 post-influenza and after other vaccines as well as bouts of various infectious diseases.
source: Studies in healthy adults have documented the importance of pTfh expansion at day 7 or day 28 post-influenza and after other vaccines as well as bouts of various infectious diseases (Bentebibel et al., 2016; Bentebibel et al., 2013; Herati et al., 2017; Herati et al., 2014; Pallikkuth et al., 2017; Pallikkuth et al., 2012; Pallikkuth et al., 2019; Boswell et al., 2014; Cubas et al., 2013; Locci et al., 2013; Simpson et al., 2010; Ueno, 2016).
evidence: This is cited from multiple references.

claim: The pTfh expansion was noted in both the DFD and STD regimens and was sustained throughout the vaccination schedule.
source: The pTfh expansion was noted in both the DFD and STD regimens and was sustained throughout the vaccination schedule.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion.

claim: Early induction of Ebola virus-specific pTfh following a single dose of the rVSV-Zaire Ebolavirus (ZEBOV) vaccine in an endemic population in Guinea was associated with protection.
source: This observation is reminiscent of the early induction of Ebola virus-specific pTfh following a single dose of the rVSV-Zaire Ebolavirus (ZEBOV) vaccine in an endemic population in Guinea, which was associated with protection (Farooq et al., 2016).
evidence: This finding is cited from Farooq et al., 2016.

claim: CXCR5 is a universally accepted receptor on pTfh cells.
source: We identified pTfh phenotypically by CXCR5 expression in memory CD4 T cells. Cellular markers that have been used to define pTfh cells and their subsets have varied, with CXCR5 being a universally accepted receptor on these cells (Vella et al., 2019; Pahwa, 2019; Bentebibel et al., 2016; Herati et al., 2017; Locci et al., 2013; Pallikkuth et al., 2012; Heit et al., 2017; He et al., 2013; Morita et al., 2011; Moysi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from multiple references.

claim: Tfh cells that are located in the GC of secondary lymphoid organs express high levels of PD-1.
source: Tfh cells that are located in the GC of secondary lymphoid organs (Vella et al., 2019; Pahwa, 2019; Herati et al., 2017; Herati et al., 2014; Heit et al., 2017) express high levels of PD-1.
evidence: This is cited from multiple references.

claim: The frequency of PD-1+ cells is very low in circulating pTfh cells.
source: The frequency of PD-1+ cells is very low in circulating pTfh cells and the use of PD-1 as an essential marker that defines pTfh is likely to limit the frequency of identifiable pTfh.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the Discussion.

claim: The use of PD-1 as an essential marker that defines pTfh is likely to limit the frequency of identifiable pTfh.
source: The frequency of PD-1+ cells is very low in circulating pTfh cells and the use of PD-1 as an essential marker that defines pTfh is likely to limit the frequency of identifiable pTfh.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the Discussion.

claim: PD-1 was found to be inhibitory for pTfh function in some studies.
source: Moreover, the relevance of PD-1-expressing pTfh remains unclear because the molecule was found to be inhibitory for pTfh function in some studies (de Armas et al., 2017a).
evidence: This finding is cited from de Armas et al., 2017a.

claim: The expression of PD-1 in combination with that of the activation markers CD38 and HLADR in pTfh is inhibitory for their function in healthy volunteers given influenza vaccine.
source: We have found that the expression of PD-1 in combination with that of the activation markers CD38 and HLADR in pTfh is inhibitory for their function in healthy volunteers given influenza vaccine (Pallikkuth et al., 2019).
evidence: This finding is cited from Pallikkuth et al., 2019.

claim: IL-21 is the signature cytokine of Tfh cells and is required for optimal B cell function.
source: IL-21 is the signature cytokine of Tfh cells and is required for optimal B cell function (Crotty, 2011; Linterman and Vinuesa, 2010; Vogelzang et al., 2008; Bryant et al., 2007; Pallikkuth and Pahwa, 2013).
evidence: This is cited from multiple references.

claim: ICOS–ICOSL interactions are important for Tfh–B cell collaboration and also for IL-21 gene transcription in Tfh cells through c-Maf.
source: Likewise, ICOS–ICOSL interactions are known to be important for Tfh–B cell collaboration and also for IL-21 gene transcription in Tfh cells through c-Maf (Bossaller et al., 2006; Bauquet et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from Bossaller et al., 2006 and Bauquet et al., 2009.

claim: IL-21 and ICOS in circulating CD4 T cells or CSP-specific pTfh are biomarkers of vaccine responses.
source: These results add to the growing body of evidence pointing to the importance of IL-21 (Schultz et al., 2016; Spensieri et al., 2016; de Armas et al., 2017b) and ICOS (Bentebibel et al., 2016; Bentebibel et al., 2013; Herati et al., 2014; Havenar-Daughton et al., 2016) in circulating CD4 T cells or CSP-specific pTfh as biomarkers of vaccine responses.
evidence: This is cited from multiple references.

claim: Neither the non-pTfh cells nor IFNγ+ CSP-specific CD4 and pTfh responses were identified as variables that were associated with protection or regimen difference in the data integration analysis.
source: In the data integration analysis, neither the non-pTfh cells nor IFNγ+ CSP-specific CD4 and pTfh responses were identified as variables that were associated with protection or regimen difference, reaffirming the central role of antigen-specific pTfh cells in the CD4 T cell compartment in the response to vaccination.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion.

claim: The development of strong, functionally competent CSP-specific memory B cells after the second dose in protected subjects suggests the development of highly Ag-experienced functional memory B cells following the early pTfh response induced by vaccination.
source: The development of strong, functionally competent CSP-specific memory B cells after the second dose in protected subjects suggests the development of highly Ag-experienced functional memory B cells following the early pTfh response induced by vaccination.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion.

claim: Development of a CSP-specific memory B cell compartment is in line with previous studies on antibody affinity, B cell somatic hypermutation, and antibody function, and suggests that affinity maturation is altered to some extent in the DFD regimen.
source: Development of a CSP-specific memory B cell compartment is in line with previous studies on antibody affinity, B cell somatic hypermutation, and antibody function, and suggests that affinity maturation is altered to some extent in the DFD regimen (Regules et al., 2016; Chaudhury et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Regules et al., 2016 and Chaudhury et al., 2017.

claim: The stronger vaccine-induced memory B cell responses elicited towards PF-16 (the C-terminus of the CSP protein) over R32LR (the central repeat region) may have played a role in protection, as this region is implicated in the initial entry of the sporozoites into hepatocytes.
source: The stronger vaccine-induced memory B cell responses elicited towards PF-16 (the C-terminus of the CSP protein) over R32LR (the central repeat region) may have played a role in protection, as this region is implicated in the initial entry of the sporozoites into hepatocytes (Ramasamy, 1998).
evidence: This is cited from Ramasamy, 1998.

claim: Vaccine-induced CSP-specific memory B cells persisted up to 159 days post-challenge, the last time point for analysis.
source: In our study, we found persistence of the vaccine-induced CSP-specific memory B cells up to 159 days post-challenge, the last time point for analysis.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion.

claim: Pepper and colleagues reported persistence of Plasmodium-specific memory B cell populations that had been induced by protein immunization up to 340 days post-infection.
source: In a previous study, Pepper and colleagues reported persistence of Plasmodium-specific memory B cell populations that had been induced by protein immunization up to 340 days post-infection (Krishnamurty et al., 2016).
evidence: This finding is cited from Krishnamurty et al., 2016.

claim: Atypical memory B cells (aMBC) were originally described as an exhausted subset of memory B cells in HIV infection.
source: Interestingly, aMBC were also increased in the DFD regimen, compared to the STD regimen, at T5 and T6. These cells, originally described as an exhausted subset of memory B cells in HIV infection (Moir and Fauci, 2009; Moir et al., 2008), have been found in the circulation of Plasmodium-infected individuals from endemic countries (Ly and Hansen, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Moir and Fauci, 2009 and Moir et al., 2008.

claim: Atypical memory B cells have been found in the circulation of Plasmodium-infected individuals from endemic countries.
source: These cells, originally described as an exhausted subset of memory B cells in HIV infection (Moir and Fauci, 2009; Moir et al., 2008), have been found in the circulation of Plasmodium-infected individuals from endemic countries (Ly and Hansen, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Ly and Hansen, 2019.

claim: A role for aMBC in malaria immunity has been suggested on the basis of the accumulation of this sub-population in situations of parasitemia or shorter exposure history in children and adults from malaria endemic areas.
source: A role for aMBC in malaria immunity has been suggested on the basis of the accumulation of this sub-population in situations of parasitemia or shorter exposure history (Weiss et al., 2009; Changrob et al., 2018) in children and adults from malaria endemic areas (Weiss et al., 2009; Changrob et al., 2018; Portugal et al., 2015); importantly, aMBC were maintained in situations of persistent parasite exposure (Ayieko et al., 2013) with a decline over 12 months in the absence of transmission.
evidence: This is cited from multiple references.

claim: aMBC were maintained in situations of persistent parasite exposure with a decline over 12 months in the absence of transmission.
source: A role for aMBC in malaria immunity has been suggested on the basis of the accumulation of this sub-population in situations of parasitemia or shorter exposure history (Weiss et al., 2009; Changrob et al., 2018) in children and adults from malaria endemic areas (Weiss et al., 2009; Changrob et al., 2018; Portugal et al., 2015); importantly, aMBC were maintained in situations of persistent parasite exposure (Ayieko et al., 2013) with a decline over 12 months in the absence of transmission.
evidence: This is cited from Ayieko et al., 2013.

claim: Non-protected participants in the STD regimen are a mix of two classes of subjects: true weak responders and strong responders that aren't protected.
source: Our results suggest that NP subjects in the STD regimen are a mix of two classes of subjects, true weak responders and strong responders that aren't protected.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion.

claim: The mixed population of non-protected subjects in the STD regimen may explain why it has been difficult to find correlates of protection in RTS,S studies.
source: This mixed population may explain why it has been difficult to find correlates of protection in RTS,S studies (Ockenhouse et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from Ockenhouse et al., 2015.

claim: In the DFD regimen, non-protected subjects are almost entirely of one class — weak responders.
source: By contrast, in the new DFD regimen, NP subjects are almost entirely of one class — weak responders.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion.

claim: The early Tfh response, induced by the initial two vaccine doses, results in the formation of a strong high-affinity memory B cell pool that is specific to CSP antigen; in the DFD, this leads to the expansion and differentiation of the pre-formed memory B cells to Ab-secreting cells.
source: On the basis of the overall findings, we suggest that the early Tfh response, induced by the initial two vaccine doses, results in the formation of a strong high-affinity memory B cell pool that is specific to CSP antigen; in the DFD, this leads to the expansion and differentiation of the pre-formed memory B cells to Ab-secreting cells.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation stated in the Discussion.

claim: In the STD vaccine regimen, early administration of the booster dose was detrimental to the expansion and differentiation of pre-formed memory B cells.
source: By contrast, in the STD vaccine regimen, early administration of the booster dose was detrimental to the expansion and differentiation of pre-formed memory B cells.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation stated in the Discussion.

claim: Previous reports found an association of CSP-specific IL-2+, TNF or IFNg+ CD4 T cells or Th1 responses with vaccine responses.
source: Previous reports found an association of CSP-specific IL-2+, TNF or IFNg+ CD4 T cells or Th1 responses with vaccine responses (Kester et al., 2009; Lumsden et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from Kester et al., 2009 and Lumsden et al., 2011.

claim: Previous studies did not examine CSP-specific pTfh within the memory CD4 T cell compartment, and most probably included both pTfh and non-pTfh cells in their analysis.
source: These studies did not examine CSP-specific pTfh within the memory CD4 T cell compartment, and most probably included both pTfh and non-pTfh cells in their analysis.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Discussion.

claim: Within the Ag-specific CD4 T cell compartment, pTfh cells but not non-pTfh show a kinetic and functional response to the malaria vaccine.
source: Our data show that within the Ag-specific CD4 T cell compartment, pTfh cells but not non-pTfh show a kinetic and functional response to the malaria vaccine.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion.

claim: Delaying and reducing the third vaccine dose is advantageous for developing a protective immune response.
source: We conclude that delaying and reducing the third vaccine dose is advantageous for developing a protective immune response.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion.

claim: The long interval between the second and third doses in the DFD regimen may be challenging in the face of overwhelming exposure to mosquitoes that can inoculate sporozoites into the host in this period, thereby affecting the development of immunity.
source: The long interval between the second and third doses may be challenging in the face of overwhelming exposure to mosquitoes that can inoculate sporozoites into the host in this period, thereby affecting the development of immunity.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Discussion.

claim: The amount of CSP delivered via natural infection is much lower than the amount of CSP in RTS,S/AS01.
source: However, the amount of CSP delivered via natural infection is much lower than the amount of CSP in RTS,S/AS01 and, thus, it is unlikely that natural infection would disrupt the development of an otherwise protective immune response.

claim: It is unlikely that natural infection would disrupt the development of an otherwise protective immune response to RTS,S/AS01.
source: However, the amount of CSP delivered via natural infection is much lower than the amount of CSP in RTS,S/AS01 and, thus, it is unlikely that natural infection would disrupt the development of an otherwise protective immune response.

claim: Children who responded well to RTS,S/AS01 vaccination had increased baseline frequencies of antibody-secreting and Tfh cells.
source: Recently, it was shown that children who responded well to RTS,S/AS01 vaccination had increased baseline frequencies of antibody-secreting and Tfh cells (Hill et al., 2020).

claim: Malaria infection may induce memory Tfh cells that have impaired B cell helper function, and may inhibit differentiation to fully functional Tfh cells, thus resulting in germinal center dysfunction and suboptimal antibody responses.
source: Nevertheless, emerging data also suggests that malaria infection may induce memory Tfh cells that have impaired B cell helper function, and may inhibit differentiation to fully functional Tfh cells, thus resulting in germinal center dysfunction and suboptimal antibody responses (Hansen et al., 2017).
evidence: This finding is cited from Hansen et al., 2017.

claim: The data indicate the generation of strong CSP-specific pTfh responses that persist even after 159 days post-challenge.
source: Last, our data indicate the generation of strong CSP-specific pTfh responses that persist even after 159 days post-challenge, suggesting that CSP-specific pTfh could serve as potential biomarkers for vaccine efficacy.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion.

claim: CSP-specific pTfh could serve as potential biomarkers for vaccine efficacy.
source: Last, our data indicate the generation of strong CSP-specific pTfh responses that persist even after 159 days post-challenge, suggesting that CSP-specific pTfh could serve as potential biomarkers for vaccine efficacy.
evidence: This is a suggestion stated in the Discussion.

claim: Monitoring CSP-specific pTfh should be considered in future malaria vaccine trials in clinical settings or field studies.
source: Monitoring CSP-specific pTfh should be considered in future malaria vaccine trials in clinical settings or field studies.
evidence: This is a recommendation stated in the Discussion.
